title: Tissues and Other Levels of Organization

Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Histology refers to the study of —
questions.answer: C

questions.answer: C

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Match: (a) Brush-bordered epithelium (b) Ciliated epithelium with (i) lining of trachea (ii) skin (iii) increasing surface area for absorption.
Fill in the blanks: Ciliated columnar epithelium is found as the lining of the ______; the matrix of cartilage is ______.
questions.answer: trachea; chondrin.

questions.q: Complete the flow chart of connective tissue: Connective tissue → A (Proper) → areolar, ______; B (Supporting) → ______, bone; C (Fluid) → ______, lymph.
questions.answer: Proper: areolar, adipose, fibrous. Supporting: cartilage, bone. Fluid: blood, lymph.

questions.q: Give the one-word term: (a) A tissue made of cells that continue to divide. (b) A tissue made of only one type of cell.
questions.answer: (a) Meristematic tissue. (b) Simple tissue.

questions.q: Name the layers of the histogen theory that give rise to (a) epidermis (b) cortex.
questions.answer: (a) Dermatogen. (b) Periblem.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Epithelial tissue has blood vessels. (b) Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the contractile proteins of muscle.
questions.answer: Actin and myosin (also troponin and tropomyosin).

questions.q: Name any two plasma proteins.
questions.answer: Fibrinogen and albumin (globulin).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Construct a flow chart using these words: xylem, complex permanent tissue, simple permanent tissue, plant tissue, meristem, parenchyma.
questions.answer: Plant tissue → Meristem; Permanent tissue → simple permanent tissue (parenchyma) and complex permanent tissue (xylem).

questions.q: Write the names of two types of complex tissues in plants and state the main function of each.
questions.answer: Xylem: conducts water and minerals upward from roots to leaves. Phloem: conducts the food prepared in the leaves to the other parts of the plant.

questions.q: Define tissue. Name the branch of biology which deals with its study.
questions.answer: A tissue is a group of cells with common origin, structure and function; the branch is histology.

questions.q: Name any two contractile proteins found in muscle fibres.
questions.answer: Actin and myosin.

questions.q: Write any two characteristics of meristematic cells.
questions.answer: They are thin-walled, undifferentiated with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus; they have no intercellular spaces and divide continuously.

questions.q: Distinguish between a simple tissue and a complex tissue.
questions.answer: A simple tissue consists of one type of cells (parenchyma); a complex tissue has more than one type of cells that work together (xylem).

questions.q: Mention two functions of epithelial tissue.
questions.answer: It covers and protects surfaces and helps in secretion and absorption.

questions.q: Name the three types of cells of blood and one function each.
questions.answer: RBCs carry oxygen and carbon dioxide; WBCs defend against germs; platelets help in clotting.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma (one point each).
questions.answer: Parenchyma: thin-walled living cells that store food. Collenchyma: living cells with corner thickening of cellulose and pectin; gives flexible support. Sclerenchyma: dead cells with lignified thick walls; gives rigidity.

questions.q: Explain the tunica-corpus theory.
questions.answer: In the shoot apex the tunica is the outer layers of cells dividing anticlinally, giving surface growth and forming the epidermis and cortex; the corpus is the inner mass dividing irregularly, giving volume growth and forming the pith and vascular tissue.

questions.q: Draw a text diagram of xylem: list its elements and state which are living and which are dead.
questions.answer: Tracheids, vessels and fibres are dead lignified cells that conduct water and give strength; xylem parenchyma is living and stores food.

questions.q: Write any three differences between skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle.
questions.answer: Skeletal: striated, voluntary, multinucleate and attached to bones. Smooth: unstriated, involuntary, uninucleate and in the walls of internal organs. Cardiac: striated, involuntary, branched with intercalated discs, found in the heart.

questions.q: Explain the structure of bone.
questions.answer: Matrix of ossein with calcium and phosphate salts; in compact bone osteocytes lie in lacunae on concentric lamellae around Haversian canals; spongy bone is at the ends; the marrow cavity makes blood cells.

questions.q: Describe the different types of epithelial tissue with one location each.
questions.answer: Squamous (lining of alveoli), cuboidal (kidney tubules), columnar (intestine), ciliated columnar (trachea) and brush-bordered (intestine, to increase surface area).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the types of meristematic tissue with their location and function.
questions.answer: Apical meristem: root and shoot tips; increases length. Intercalary meristem: at the bases of leaves or internodes; increases internode length. Lateral meristem: cambium and cork cambium; increases thickness (secondary growth).

questions.q: Explain the structure and function of xylem and phloem.
questions.answer: Xylem: tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma; conducts water and minerals upward. Phloem: sieve tubes, companion cells, fibres and parenchyma; conducts food from the leaves to the other parts.

questions.q: Describe the connective tissues of animals.
questions.answer: Proper (areolar, adipose, fibrous), supporting (cartilage and bone) and fluid (blood and lymph) with their cells, matrix and functions.

questions.q: Explain the histogen theory.
questions.answer: The promeristem at the apex differentiates into dermatogen (epidermis or epiblema), periblem (cortex) and plerome (pericycle, pith and vascular tissue).
